summary: Banked a code-only deletion journal adapter candidate under internal/hosted/deletion. This is not task acceptance, production wiring, AWS qualification, or deployment approval.
implemented: Selective port of the historical S3 object-store adapter, hash-chained generation journal, explicit filesystem fake, focused package tests, and opt-in S3 qualification test.

Strict journal-object decoding and validation: canonical JSON with no unknown fields; positive matching coordinates; non-empty writer identity; UTC timestamp; correctly shaped predecessor hash; known entry/seal kind; valid opaque entry payload; and empty deletion payload on seals.
Resume-watermark validation now rejects an object whose embedded generation/sequence do not match the referenced key, as well as malformed/unknown entries and seals.

ReadThrough now rejects any visible same-generation tail after a seal watermark (including malformed objects and delete markers), and fails incomplete when a later generation is visible beyond a missing intermediate generation. Valid contiguous successors remain readable.

verification.red_baseline: Before the validator patch, the focused malformed-record tests ran against the original adapter and all five then-present cases failed at runtime: ReadThrough returned nil error for unknown kind, invalid entry payload, malformed seal payload, mismatched resume coordinates, and unknown kind at the resume position.
verification.focused_green: go test -mod=mod -modfile=/Volumes/BuildOffload/tmp/t23-48-journal-port-20261001/module-proof/verify.mod ./internal/hosted/deletion -run '^TestReadThroughRejectsMalformed' -count=1 passed after the patch; the suite now covers seven malformed zero/resume-watermark cases.
verification.aws_calls: None. SERENITY_T2348_S3_QUALIFY was explicitly empty; TestS3Qualification was skipped.
verification.seal_and_generation_red_baseline: Against banked strict-validation commit 82763466b4b33679508350803041b327c458e8f7, runtime regressions reproduced: a valid same-generation post-seal entry was accepted; malformed and delete-marker tails returned incomplete instead of fence-violated; and a visible generation 3 after absent generation 2 was accepted.
verification.seal_and_generation_green: Focused regressions plus TestJournalContract passed. Cases cover valid/malformed/delete-marker same-generation tails after a resumed seal; gap detection from zero and from a seal; and valid contiguous successors above configured generation.

remaining: Current main service/gateway/backup and partner-aware assembly wiring is untouched; integrate only after coordinator review and preserve current contracts and billing interfaces.

NewAWSJournal still uses the AWS SDK default credential chain. The app service denies IMDS; retain that deny and require a separately reviewed, explicitly scoped credential source before deployment. No credential or IAM workaround is part of this candidate.

T23.54 must provide the dedicated versioned journal bucket, conditional-create policy, deny-delete policy, retained lifecycle configuration, least-privilege IAM, and runtime bucket/region configuration.
T23.47 live billing closure qualification and the T23.50 cross-host activation fence/credential-revocation proof remain independent gates.
The historical disposable S3 receipt is not re-run or treated as current stack/IAM qualification.

A visible generation after a missing intermediate generation is rejected. If later configured generations are empty/invisible, ReadThrough returns the older seal it actually reached; this library behavior does not establish that seal as the adopted/current generation for T23.50. Expected-generation adoption remains a separate activation gate.
production_merge_gate: HOLD: banked candidate only; not merged or accepted
